items.title: Seal at leaf zero accepts any agreed-state proof: Dave _requireAgreeState and prt.lua validate_seal_response never look at the proof argument when the divergence is at leaf 0
items.component: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 prt/contracts Match.sol _requireAgreeState (via Tournament.sealLeafMatch / sealInnerMatchAndCreateInnerTournament); doc/recipes/prt.lua validate_seal_response
items.role: Referee model (Dave as the deployed referee; prt.lua as the recipe referee model)
items.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no; trigger is a claimant's seal move ('dishonest claimants (any number, any logs, any proofs, any timing)'). 2 Role: Dave and prt.lua are Referee model (AUDIT table); section 3 'A defect in what it accepts or derives is rated as if a deployed referee had it.' 3 Medium case: 'A referee verifier that accepts trailing data that does not affect its result (R3)'; R3 lists 'trailing data' among log validity conditions. Same reading split as the confirmed R1-R3-3 (Medium / Low), at a different site with a different fix. Alternative Low: the trailing-data case covers transition-log verifiers only, not the computation-hash proof checks of the tournament. 4 Critical: no; the sealed divergence (agree state = initial hash, contested leaves) is unchanged. Code checked: Match.sol l.297-303 returns before using agreeStateProof; prt.lua 310-339 ignores response.agreed_state_hash_proof when leaf_index == 0.
items.reason: Code confirmed: both referees ignore the proof argument at leaf 0. Medium by 'A referee verifier that accepts trailing data that does not affect its result (R3)' as for R1-R3-3; Low if that case covers only transition-log verifiers.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: when a bisection converges on leaf 0, both referees accept a seal whatever its agreed-state proof holds. Dave (bugs/harness/work/dave/released/prt/contracts/src/tournament/libs/Match.sol, _requireAgreeState l.290-303): 'if (divergencePosition == 0) { require(agreeState.eq(args.initialHash)); return; }' never reads agreeStateProof; for a non-zero position it demands exactly `height` siblings. Reached from Tournament.sealLeafMatch and sealInnerMatchAndCreateInnerTournament. Recipe referee model (doc/recipes/prt.lua validate_seal_response, l.310-339): the proof is checked only when leaf_index ~= 0; at leaf 0 response.agreed_state_hash_proof is ignored (any table, any content). Trigger: any claimant seals a match whose first divergent leaf is 0 (a claim that lies about its first sampled state; the common uarch first-step dispute) and attaches a junk or oversized proof. Required behavior: THREAT_MODEL R3 'Conditions on the log are validity conditions. A log that fails one must be rejected. Examples are wrong order, wrong address, wrong size, duplicate, missing, or trailing data'; section 4 'A verifier must assume that every count, index, address, size, and hash it receives was chosen to fool it'; section 3 Referee model 'A defect in what it accepts or derives is rated as if a deployed referee had it'; section 8 Medium 'A referee verifier that accepts trailing data that does not affect its result (R3)'. Sibling confirmed bug: R1-R3-3 (prt.lua accepts superfluous logs in state-transition proofs). Test idea (model, cheapest): require('prt'), build a height-1 match at position 0 whose left leaves differ, call validate_seal_response with a non-empty junk agreed_state_hash_proof (e.g. sibling_hashes={'not','a','proof'}) and assert it raises; exit 1 while it returns a divergence; a control with a nil/empty proof must still be accepted. Optional Dave part on the released-contracts local chain: drive a match to READY_TO_SEAL at runningLeafPosition 0 and call sealLeafMatch with _agreeHash=initialHash and a non-empty _agreeHashProof (e.g. 1000 random words); assert revert. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r7/MANTOURN/seal0.lua (output 'seal at leaf zero with a junk agreed-state proof accepted: true 0 true'). Dave part was read only, not executed.

items.title: Manual's output verifier (verify-output-proof.lua) and the CLI's read_proof execute proof files as Lua chunks: a crafted proof hangs the verifier or allocates without bound
items.component: doc/recipes/verify-output-proof.lua read_proof (printed in the manual under 'Output verification'); src/cartesi-machine.lua read_proof (default 'lua' proof format, --cmio-advance-state=last_output_proof)
items.role: Support (manual recipe stands in for the referee's output validation, A5; CLI stands in for the honest operator)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: not excluded; the data is a proof file, and section 4 says 'Logs and proofs are adversarial'. Not an untrusted machine-API caller. 2 Role: Support (AUDIT table). Section 3: 'Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as a referee verifier for a copy of a verifier'. 3 In the stood-in role this is an unbounded verifier on adversarial data: section 4 'Every path that carries such data must be memory-safe and bounded'; High 'A crash, hang, memory-safety defect or unbounded allocation in a component in the honest-operator role, caused by data from other parties that the honest operator may decline'. So Medium for the support copy. 4 Not Critical: the PRT referee model and Dave take proofs as JSON schema / calldata. 5 Alternative Low: if the script and CLI option consume only the operator's own artifacts ('a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller'). Code checked: verify-output-proof.lua l.11-13 'assert(loadfile(name, "t", {}))()'.
items.reason: Code confirmed: proofs are executed as Lua. Stand-in High ('crash, hang ... or unbounded allocation ... caused by data from other parties that the honest operator may decline') gives Medium for support; Low if only own artifacts are read.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: the manual's reference output verifier doc/recipes/verify-output-proof.lua (printed in doc/README.md ~8914-8982, presented as the way to check an output 'from the settled state hash and those artifacts alone') reads each proof with read_proof(name) = assert(loadfile(name, 't', {}))() (recipe l.11-13), i.e. it executes the proof file as Lua. An empty environment removes globals but not loops or the string metatable, so a proof file 'while true do end' hangs it and 'return { iflags_y_data = ("x"):rep(1 << 34) }' allocates 16 GiB, both before any check of the proof runs. The CLI has the same reader: src/cartesi-machine.lua read_proof (~3446-3450, load(contents, filename, 't', {})) with default format 'lua' (resolve_format ~1317-1324), used by --cmio-advance-state=last_output_proof:<file>. A safe decoder exists (cartesi.fromjson(contents, 'Proof')). Trigger: a party verifies an output proof or outputs-root proof received from another party (the prover who wants the output accepted). Required behavior: THREAT_MODEL section 4 'Logs and proofs are adversarial. A verifier must assume that every count, index, address, size, and hash it receives was chosen to fool it' and 'Every path that carries such data must be memory-safe and bounded, and must report errors without terminating the process'; section 8 High 'A crash, hang, memory-safety defect or unbounded allocation in a component in the honest-operator role, caused by data from other parties that the honest operator may decline'; section 3 support rule 'Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as a referee verifier for a copy of a verifier'. Test idea (bugs/<ID>/test.sh): write loop.lua ('while true do end') and big.lua (2^34-byte string); run lua5.4 doc/recipes/verify-output-proof.lua <hash.bin> <proof> <proof2> <out.bin> under 'timeout 10' and 'ulimit -v 4000000'; required: prompt non-zero exit with an error message, no timeout, no memory exhaustion; exit 1 on timeout (124) or 'not enough memory'. Optional second case for the CLI's last_output_proof with the default format. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r7/MANHASHCOMP/vop/ (loop.lua killed by timeout 5, exit 124; big.lua 'not enough memory' under ulimit).

items.title: Manual's slicing/splicing verification binds the proof neither to the known state hash M nor to the drive's address and size: verify_slice/verify_splice and the instantiation/extraction recipes accept a forged M' or a 'result' read from another node
items.component: Lua helper library cartesi.hash-tree verify_slice/verify_splice; doc/recipes/splice-calculator-with-new-drive.lua and slice-calculator-output.lua; manual 'Slicing and splicing', 'Template instantiation', 'Result extraction'
items.role: Support (helper library and demo recipes standing in for the proof verifier the manual calls 'the blockchain way')
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: no; adversarial proof data given to a verifier built as the manual says. 2 Role: Support; the PRT referee model calls verify_slice but checks root_hash, target_address and sizes itself, so the most critical component reaching the defect is the recipe/library as a copy of a node-proof verifier. Section 3: 'Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as a referee verifier for a copy of a verifier.' 3/4 In the stood-in verifier role: section 1 soundness 'a proof verifier accepts a node that the committed tree does not hold at the stated index and height'; R11 'Every referee parameter comes from the referee, never from the proof' (index, height and root are referee parameters per section 2); readings.md: violating a rule's wording in the stood-in role is Critical there, hence Medium. Also a manual contradiction on a soundness point: the manual says 'the code first checks the root hash M against the one found in the proof' (doc/README.md 8340) but verify_slice never receives M. 5 Alternative Low: the 'Hash-view of state' recipes are off-chain illustrations, no in-scope verifier is stood in for (result extraction via NVRAM is not the A5 output path).
items.reason: Code and manual confirmed: verify_slice compares only with proof.root_hash; recipes check only log2_root_size. Stand-in verifier violates section 1 soundness / R11, so Medium for support; Low if the recipes stand in for no in-scope verifier.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: src/cartesi/hash-tree.lua verify_slice (l.31-38) checks the proof only against its own proof.root_hash; verify_splice (l.41-44) adds roll(new_target_hash) == new_root_hash; neither takes the expected root M nor checks target_address/log2_target_size. The manual (doc/README.md 8336-8351) states 'To verify a slicing operation, the code first checks the root hash M against the one found in the proof' and that splicing 'first ... verifies that the slicing operation is valid. This ensures that the sibling hashes are correct'. The recipes doing 'the blockchain way' add nothing: doc/recipes/splice-calculator-with-new-drive.lua (l.26-33) checks only template_input_proof.log2_root_size == 64, never proof.root_hash == template hash M nor its address/size; doc/recipes/slice-calculator-output.lua (l.30-39) checks only output_proof.log2_root_size, never target_address == output_nvram.start or log2_target_size == output_nvram.log2_size, nor that M' is halted/yielded. The manual (8544-8552) says this 'confirms that an output NVRAM with exactly this content sits in the machine whose state hash is M''. Trigger: a dishonest prover gives (a) a 'pristine input proof' with arbitrary siblings and root_hash = roll(siblings, arbitrary target), so verify_splice confirms any M' it picks; or (b) a whole-machine proof of another same-size node (e.g. the input NVRAM, whose contents the instantiator chose) with that node's contents as the 'result'. Required behavior: THREAT_MODEL section 1 soundness 'a proof verifier accepts a node that the committed tree does not hold at the stated index and height' is a soundness failure; R11 'Every referee parameter comes from the referee, never from the proof' (section 2: index, height and root of each authenticated node are referee parameters); section 4 'Logs and proofs are adversarial'; section 8 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point ... takes the severity it would have if the manual were right'; section 3 support rule 'Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as a referee verifier for a copy of a verifier'. Not affected: prt.lua and game-output.lua check root/address/size themselves. Test idea (bugs/<ID>/test.lua): synthetic machine {ram 1 MiB, nvram input @0xa0000000 4 KiB, nvram output @0xb0000000 4 KiB}; implement instantiate/extract exactly as the recipes do; require that (1) a proof whose root_hash differs from M is refused and (2) a proof targeting the input NVRAM offered as the output proof is refused; exit 1 while either is accepted. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r7/MANHASHSTATE/splice-forge.lua (output 'instantiation: verify_splice accepts forged M': true  M' == real instantiated hash: false'; 'extraction: verify_splice accepts result "1+1\n" from output nvram: true').

items.title: Manual's specification of advance-state delivery omits state writes the transition makes (imcyclemax = mcycle + 2^48 - 1, zero padding of the rx buffer): the documented host loop yields a different state hash than send_cmio_response
items.component: Manual doc/README.md ('#### Rollup' host loop and prose, register list, send_cmio_response API text) vs input delivery (src/send-cmio-response.cpp, shared by all paths and the regenerated SendCmioResponse.sol)
items.role: Honest operator (input delivery); manual as the specification
items.severity: Medium / Low; Critical under the literal 'manual defines the transition function' reading
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: no; it concerns delivery on the honest operator's path ('Delivering inputs'). 2 Role: input delivery is Honest operator (AUDIT table); the regenerated step agrees with it, so the disagreement is with the manual only. 3 Medium: 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point ... takes the severity it would have if the manual were right'; if the manual's four-write delivery were right, every implemented path deviates together: 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths' (Medium). Security-relevant: imcyclemax is a fixed-point register (R5), and the rx buffer is in R7's list; R13 makes 'The accesses each logged transition makes' part of the protocol. 4 Critical only under the literal reading of section 2 'The manual's documented semantics define it [the state transition function]' with R3, or literal R7 for the rx-buffer padding. 5 Low if the blockchain chapter's 'each input owns 2^48 mcycles, counted from the state that receives it' counts as documenting the write and the host loop is read as illustrative (silence, not contradiction; cf. R1-R14-2). Manual checked: doc/README.md 7790-7799 lists four writes; 7855-7861 prose likewise; no sentence says delivery sets imcyclemax.
items.reason: Manual's delivery description (host loop, prose, API text) lists four writes; implementation also writes imcyclemax and zero-pads rx. Medium by the manual-contradiction clause plus the consistent-deviation case; Low if read as an incomplete illustration.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: the manual describes an advance-state delivery as exactly four state changes and never says it writes imcyclemax or zero-pads the rx buffer. doc/README.md 7790-7799 (host loop): 'Write the current state hash to the state at AR_SHADOW_REVERT_ROOT_HASH_START / Write ABI-encoded EvmAdvance(...) to CMIO RX buffer and its length to length / Write HTIF_YIELD_REASON_ADVANCE_STATE to REASON and length as DATA in fromhost / Reset register iflags_Y to 0'; 7855-7861: 'The call also writes the request to the CMIO RX buffer and its type and length to the HTIF register fromhost, and unblocks the machine by clearing its iflags_Y register'; 4944-4957 (API text) likewise; 7384-7385 only says imcyclemax 'holds the inclusive mcycle limit'. Implementation (src/send-cmio-response.cpp l.66-76 writeImcyclemax and writeMemoryWithPadding; src/state-access.hpp 450-463; regenerated SendCmioResponse.sol l.93) also sets imcyclemax = mcycle + 2^48 - 1 (saturating) and zero-fills the rx buffer from the input's end to the next power of two (min 32 bytes). Both are hashed, so following the manual gives a different state hash. Trigger: every state-changing advance delivery; visible to anyone implementing delivery from the manual (second node, auditor of SendCmioResponse.sol). Required behavior: THREAT_MODEL intro 'The emulator's user manual is the specification it refers to'; section 2 'State transition function ... The manual's documented semantics define it on every state'; R7 'The emulator implements the RISC-V specification and the devices as the manual documents them, departing only where the manual documents a deviation' with 'The rx buffer, the tx buffer, and the yield interface (contents, lengths, and reason encoding)'; section 8 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right'; section 8 Medium 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths'. Test idea (Lua): on bugs/harness/work/configs/baremetal-template/machine, copy A gets send_cmio_response(ADVANCE_STATE, input, root); copy B gets exactly the manual's four writes (write_memory revert root hash, write_memory rx buffer with the input, write_reg htif_fromhost, write_reg iflags_Y 0); assert equal root hashes (fails: imcyclemax 0x100000035cee3 vs 0xffffffffffffffff; with a prior longer input the padding bytes differ too). Alternatively assert that every address log_send_cmio_response writes (including imcyclemax at 0x2f8) is named in the manual's delivery description. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r7/MANARCH/deliver.lua (roots b6d9e351... vs 46e884f7...; equal after also writing imcyclemax).

items.title: Manual says the processor shadow and shadow TLB are ranges visible to the main processor and described by PMA entries; the emulator gives them no PMA entry and every guest access faults
items.component: Manual doc/README.md ('The main processor', 'The board', 'Address ranges', 'PMAs') vs machine address ranges / interpreter (src/machine-address-ranges.cpp shadow state registered with .pmas = false)
items.severity: Medium / Low; Critical under the literal R7 reading
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: no. 2 Role: interpreter and state layout, Honest operator. 3 Medium: manual-contradiction clause; if the manual were right (shadow ranges visible read-only with PMA entries), the emulator's refusal is 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths'. Security-relevant: it is the R8 containment boundary ('Guest memory accesses cannot address the processor registers ... the revert root hash, imcyclemax'), so the manual, not the code, is likely wrong, but the clause rates as if the manual were right. Same family as confirmed R3-VARSPEC-1 (Medium / Critical literal). 4 Critical under literal R7 ('Address translation and memory permissions ... any deviation lets an input subvert a correct guest'). 5 Low if 'externally' and the Address-ranges sentence are read loosely. Manual checked: 7337-7339 'makes its entire state available, externally and read-only, by mapping every register to the start of the physical address space'; 7445-7446 board table lists 0x0-0xfff and 0x1000-0x6fff; 7875-7880 'The address ranges visible to the main processor ... These are the ranges listed in the board mapping table ... and discoverable at runtime via the PMA array', with only the uarch ranges called private.
items.reason: Manual text confirmed (board table + 'ranges visible to the main processor ... listed in the board mapping table ... discoverable via the PMA array'); emulator has no PMA entry and faults. Medium via manual-contradiction clause, as R3-VARSPEC-1.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: the manual says the processor/board shadow (0x0-0xfff) and the shadow TLB (0x1000-0x6fff) are address ranges visible to the main processor, each described by a PMA entry, and that every register is mapped read-only at the start of the physical address space; the emulator registers the shadow state (0x0-0x7fff) with the hash tree only (src/machine-address-ranges.cpp ~315-318, .pmas = false), so the guest-readable PMA array at 0x10000 has no entry for it and any guest load there raises a load access fault. Manual: doc/README.md 7337-7339 ('The processor makes its entire state available, externally and read-only, by mapping every register to the start of the physical address space (in the processor shadow, a 4KiB range)'); 7445-7446 (board table rows 'Processor and board shadow', 'Shadow TLB'); 7875-7880 ('The address ranges visible to the main processor are mapped at fixed positions ... These are the ranges listed in the board mapping table ... and discoverable at runtime via the PMA array'); 7884-7890 (only the uarch shadow and uarch RAM are called private); 7896-7898 ('Each address range visible to the main processor is described by an entry in the array of Physical Memory Attribute records'); DID table with PMA_SHADOW_STATE_DID = 2. Trigger: guest code that follows the manual and reads a register from the shadow (e.g. imcyclemax at 0x2f8) or looks for the shadow in the PMA array. Required behavior: THREAT_MODEL R7 'The emulator implements the RISC-V specification and the devices as the manual documents them, departing only where the manual documents a deviation' (area 'Address translation and memory permissions'); section 8 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right'; Medium 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths'. Note R8 requires the code's behavior, so the expected fix is likely the manual; the test must pass for either fix (e.g. assert that either a PMA entry covers 0x0 and a guest load succeeds, or the manual lists these ranges as invisible to the main processor). Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r7/MANARCH/g/probe.c and g/run.lua (loads at 0x0, 0x100, 0xfe0, 0x1000, 0x7000 give mcause 5; 0x10000 reads 0x800000fd), /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r7/MANARCH/pmas.lua (9 PMA entries, none with start 0 or DID 2) on bugs/harness/work/configs/linux-rootfs.

items.title: Uarch memory map: manual says the uarch can access all memory ranges and devices of the main processor; natively uarch loads from device ranges and holes return 0 on every path (store part is R1-R10-1)
items.component: Manual doc/README.md 'The microarchitecture' vs uarch memory access (src/machine.cpp read_word/write_word, uarch state access, log producers, replay verifier, regenerated step)
items.role: Honest operator (uarch, log producers); Referee verifier if the verifiers accept the loads as described
items.severity: High (if loads outside the documented uarch memory map are uarch traps that verifiers accept, R3) / Medium (manual contradiction, consistent deviation) / Low
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: no (machine API was used only to build an unreachable uarch state; the contradiction itself needs no API misuse). 2 Role: uarch/log producers Honest operator; verifiers Referee verifier. Store part: same root cause and fix as confirmed R1-R10-1 (verifiers accept stores native refuses) and is folded there. 3 Load part: R3 defines a uarch trap as 'an access that its memory map does not allow'. If the manual's map (main-processor ranges and devices plus private RAM) is the map, a load from a hole is a trap; native defines a successor (0) instead of refusing, and the replay verifier accepts it although the log authenticates the address: High 'A verifier that misbehaves only on demonstrably unreachable before-states ... (such as accepting a uarch trap, R3)'. Loads from device addresses returning 0 instead of the device register: manual contradiction, Medium 'undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths' (readings.md: that case has no reachability condition). Unreachability argument (hunter): the pristine uarch program uses only shadow-register addresses and main-processor memory, the uarch RAM is not guest-addressable and each mcycle ends with the reset. 4 Critical: no (unreachable). 5 Low if the manual sentence is satisfied by access through the shadows and uarch-internal behavior is not covered by the deviation case.
items.reason: Load/hole part is distinct from R1-R10-1 (native itself defines a successor; different fix). High if hole loads are traps per R3's 'memory map' and verifiers accept them; Medium as consistent deviation from the manual; Low under loose reading. Unsure, kept.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect (load part; the store part is confirmed R1-R10-1 and must not be re-proved): the manual's only statement of the uarch memory map (doc/README.md 7393-7397 'code running in the uarch has access to the entire state of the Cartesi Machine, including the main processor and the entire board'; 7429-7430 'In addition to being able to access all memory ranges and devices visible to the main processor, the uarch includes a private 2MiB of RAM') says the uarch can access the main processor's ranges and devices. Natively a uarch LD from a device address (HTIF 0x40008000, CLINT, PLIC) returns 0, not the device register (with htif_tohost = 0x0101000000000041, LD 0x40008000 gives 0 while LD from its shadow address 0x330 gives the value), and an LD from an unmapped hole or any address up to 0xfffffffffffffff8 also returns 0; log_step_uarch logs these and verify_step_uarch accepts them. Required behavior: THREAT_MODEL R3 'The uarch traps when it executes ... an access that its memory map does not allow'; 'Running the uarch natively, the computation-hash builders and the log producers refuse every uarch trap instead of defining a successor. A verifier refuses a trap whenever the log it receives already authenticates the condition'; section 8 High 'A verifier that misbehaves only on demonstrably unreachable before-states ... (such as accepting a uarch trap, R3)'; R7 / section 8 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point ... takes the severity it would have if the manual were right'. Reachability: needs a non-pristine uarch program (unreachable from a valid template; build it with write_memory on uarch RAM as for R1-R10-1). Test idea: patch uarch RAM with 'ld x5,0(x6)' and x6 = (a) an unmapped hole (e.g. 0x8000 region outside any range, or 0x1000000000) and (b) AR_HTIF_START; run one run_uarch step, one log_step_uarch + verify_step_uarch, and if cheap the EVM step harness; assert that either all refuse (trap) for the hole, and for the device address return the device register value as the manual says, or that the manual documents the uarch memory map the code implements (decide which outcome the test asserts from the manual's wording; prefer asserting the R3 trap refusal for holes since no documented range covers them). items.title: Stored revert mode: a host I/O error inside a commit makes the CLI's error-path revert delete the synced <dir> (and on a failed rename every copy of the committed state)
items.component: cartesi-machine CLI --revert-mode=stored (src/cartesi-machine.lua revert_stored commit 3893-3918, revert 3920-3929, __close 3941-3943)
items.role: Support (CLI; stands in for an operator implementation that retains its machine)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: the host-fault exclusion holds only 'as long as the emulator does not turn them into a wrong hash, a wrong proof, or a directory that O2 guarantees but that later loads as a different state'; here the tool's own cleanup deletes O2-guaranteed directories (destroyed, then synced) in a running process, which section 5 forbids: 'A defect ... that damages a directory while O2 guarantees it, is not excused'. Literal reading: deletion is not 'loads as a different state', so excluded. 2 Role: CLI Support; stands in for the honest operator. 3 The Medium persistence case requires 'without a wrong hash or damage to a directory that O2 guarantees', so it does not cap. 4 In the stood-in role: O2 binds the tools ('The tools and reference implementations that ship with it must follow them'), R4 'After a stop, it restarts from a directory that O2 guarantees' becomes impossible: Critical there, Medium for support. 5 Low if CLI stored mode is a pure development tool. Distinct from R5-INVSTORE-2 (crash + recovery rule; its rename-before-remove fix leaves this error path intact) and from R6-DYNPERSIST-1 (remove/rename reporting). Code checked: commit removes the backup, sets backup_directory=nil, on rename failure removes .tmp and rethrows with snapshot_taken still true; __close -> revert removes <dir> then clones from backup_directory.
items.reason: Code confirmed: after a failure past the backup removal, __close->revert deletes the synced <dir> and the clone from the (gone or nil) backup fails. Stand-in O2/R4 violation gives support Medium; OOS/Low under the literal host-fault reading or dev-tool reading.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: in src/cartesi-machine.lua stored revert mode, revert_stored.__index:commit (l.3893-3918) destroys the machine, syncs <dir> (now O2-guaranteed with the newly accepted state), clones it to <dir>.revert.tmp and syncs it, then m:remove_stored(<dir>.revert) and sets self.backup_directory = nil, then try_rename_stored(.tmp -> .revert); on rename failure it calls m:remove_stored(<dir>.revert.tmp) and rethrows. snapshot_taken is still true, so the to-be-closed backup runs __close(err) (l.3941-3943) -> revert() (l.3920-3929), which unconditionally does m:destroy(); m:remove_stored(<dir>) and only then m:clone_stored(self.backup_directory, <dir>), which fails ('bad argument #1 to clone_stored (string expected, got nil)', or ENOENT from a half-removed backup), after the synced <dir> is gone. Rename-failure case: <dir>, <dir>.revert and <dir>.revert.tmp all gone. Unlink-failure case (EIO inside remove_stored of .revert): <dir> gone, half-removed .revert, good .tmp, and the documented recovery rule ('If machine.revert exists, it holds that state, so discard machine and machine.revert.tmp') discards the only intact copy. Trigger: a host I/O fault (EIO, ENOSPC/EDQUOT, failed directory fsync) during the commit after an accepted input of `cartesi-machine --revert-mode=stored --load=<dir>,clone:<template>,sharing:all --cmio-advance-state=...`, after backup removal starts; the process keeps running. Required behavior: THREAT_MODEL section 4 'A host fault ... may stop the honest operator, but the emulator must never turn one into a wrong hash, a wrong proof, or a directory that O2 guarantees but that later loads as a different state'; section 5 'O1 and O2 bind the emulator too. The tools and reference implementations that ship with it must follow them ... A defect ... that damages a directory while O2 guarantees it, is not excused by them'; R4 'After a stop, it restarts from a directory that O2 guarantees and keeps defending its claim'; section 3 support rule 'Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'. Manual promise: '<dir>.revert always holds a synced copy of the last committed state'. Distinct from confirmed R5-INVSTORE-2 (stop + recovery rule; its rename-before-remove fix does not change revert()'s delete-then-clone); the test must fail with R5-INVSTORE-2's fix applied. Test idea (bugs/<ID>/test.sh): build an LD_PRELOAD shim failing the 3rd renameat2() with EIO (and a second case failing the Nth unlink under *.revert/ during input 0's commit); run the stored-mode epoch on bugs/harness/work/configs/baremetal-template with 2 accepted inputs; then apply the manual's recovery rule to what is on disk and assert the selected directory loads with the root after input 0 or the committed state before it; exit 1 when nothing loadable remains or the rule selects a half-removed .revert. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r7/MANCLIROLL/failrename.c, failunlink.c, fi/ (after the run fi/m, fi/m.revert, fi/m.revert.tmp absent; unlink case: m.revert does not load, m.revert.tmp holds mcycle 8506023, 0x8500ec6c...).

items.title: Documented uarch computation-hash shortcut (begin_epoch:false + next_input_offset, 'needs no epoch files') aborts with 'outputs Merkle root mismatch' and no claim whenever the application accepted any earlier output
items.component: cartesi-machine CLI --uarch-cycle-computation-hash with --cmio-advance-state=begin_epoch:false,next_input_offset (initialize_cmio_outputs 3533-3557, flush_pending_outputs 3679-3697, run_advance_state_input 4718-4727) vs doc/README.md ~2686-2715
items.role: Support (CLI as a tool that computes uarch-level claims)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: no; the application is correctly designed and the command is the manual's. 2 Role: Support; 'Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for ... a tool that computes claims'. 3 Manual contradiction on a claim-computation point ('takes the severity it would have if the manual were right'): the manual says the shortcut 'needs no epoch files' and starts at the input. 4 Stood-in role: R4 'From any reachable state ... the honest operator can always compute the claim' broken for any app with prior outputs: Critical, so Medium. 5 Alternative Low: as triage dropped R5-INVBRIDGE-3, the check is a documented opt-out (check_outputs_merkle_root:false or outputs_frontier/last_output_proof), so the claim stays computable. Distinct from R5-INVBRIDGE-3 (guest root differs; here the guest is honest and the CLI's host frontier starts empty in a documented mode) and R4-RGPLAYERGUEST-1 (outputs-root length).
items.reason: Documented shortcut fails for every correctly designed app with prior outputs; stand-in R4 Critical gives support Medium; Low under the R5-INVBRIDGE-3 opt-out reading. Unsure, kept.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: doc/README.md ~2686-2715 documents a shortcut for uarch computation hashes in a later input: 'The uarch cycle computation hash needs no epoch files ... Given a machine at the state that receives that input, begin_epoch:false with next_input_offset set to the input's zero-based offset in the epoch ... starts there'. In that mode src/cartesi-machine.lua initialize_cmio_outputs (3533-3557) starts an empty host outputs frontier (no outputs_frontier/last_output_proof given), while the guest's tx-buffer root commits to all outputs accepted before input k. At input k's rx-accepted yield, flush_pending_outputs (3679-3697, check_outputs_merkle_root defaults true) fails 'outputs Merkle root mismatch at input k' and the process exits 1. If the target period lies after the input's stop, completed in uarch_cycle_computation_hash_end_input (4458-4473) after the flush, no claim is printed; if inside the input, the hash is printed but exit is 1. The manual does not mention outputs_frontier/last_output_proof or check_outputs_merkle_root:false; the help says the host tree 'start[s] empty at genesis'. Trigger: any correctly designed application with at least one output accepted before the target input; operator runs the documented shortcut. Required behavior: THREAT_MODEL R4 'From any reachable state, at the position where it is reached, the honest operator can always compute the claim'; section 8 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point ... takes the severity it would have if the manual were right'; section 3 support rule 'Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for ... a tool that computes claims'. Related but distinct: R5-INVBRIDGE-3 (dropped: abort on a guest whose root differs, documented opt-out) and R4-RGPLAYERGUEST-1 (confirmed). Test idea (bugs/<ID>/test.sh): from bugs/harness/work/configs/baremetal-template, deliver input 0 that emits one output and is accepted; --store the machine; run the manual's shortcut (--load=after0 --cmio-advance-state=input_file_index_begin:1,input_file_index_end:2,output_proof:,begin_epoch:false,next_input_offset:1 --uarch-cycle-computation-hash=log2_mcycle_period:10,mcycle_period_index:2^38+100000); assert exit 0 and a hash equal to the from-template run with begin_epoch:true over inputs 0..1 (reference 0xad98ec94...). Today: exit 1, no hash. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r7/MANCLIROLL/u/.

items.title: get_initial_config() of a loaded machine (and the stored config.json) reports creation-time register values, contrary to the manual's 'the values of all registers will reflect the values as they were when stored'
items.component: Machine API machine::store / machine_config::store / get_initial_config (C, Lua, JSON-RPC)
items.role: Honest operator for store (on the path: 'Storing and reloading the machine'); get_initial_config readers are support/diagnostic. Both ratings given.
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: no exclusion needed (guest-changed registers such as mcycle, pc, imcyclemax go stale without any write_reg). 2 Role: store is honest operator; no in-tree operator path reads stale registers (CLI reads only iunrep, which load validates, and htif fields, which the guest cannot change); prt.lua does not call get_initial_config. 3 Manual statement confirmed at doc/README.md 4129-4136: 'Likewise, the values of all registers will reflect the values as they were when stored.' Medium reading: section 8 Medium 'A machine API operation ... that, used as documented, leaves ... a stored directory inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9)' plus the manual-contradiction clause (if the manual were right, a tool checking 'waiting at a manual yield with the accepted reason' through the config would be right; today it is wrong). Low reading: config register fields are never read for a transition or hash (R2 'one source of truth' holds), R9 concerns hashes, so it is a non-security documentation contradiction. 4 Critical: no rule violated at a reachable state. 5 Low otherwise.
items.reason: Manual explicitly promises stored register values; config.json/get_initial_config keep creation values. Medium under the R9 'stored directory inconsistent' case with the manual clause; Low if unread config fields are not security-relevant. Unsure, kept.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: doc/README.md 4129-4136 says of a machine loaded from a directory that get_initial_config() returns the configuration used to instantiate the stored copy and 'Likewise, the values of all registers will reflect the values as they were when stored.' machine::store (src/machine.cpp ~520, m_c.store(dir)) writes the creation-time config m_c to config.json without refreshing processor.registers / uarch registers from the shadow state, and machine::get_initial_config (~404) returns it, so after create -> run -> store -> load, get_initial_config().processor.registers.mcycle/pc/imcyclemax/iflags are the first-creation values while read_reg gives the stored ones; only iunrep is cross-checked (validate_processor_shadow). Trigger: any caller that reads registers from get_initial_config of a loaded machine (e.g. a tool checking that an adopted template waits at an accepted manual yield). Required behavior: THREAT_MODEL section 8 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right'; section 8 Medium 'A machine API operation off the honest operator's path that, used as documented, leaves the hash tree, the cached state of the machine or a stored directory inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9)'; R2 'Every register ... has one source of truth in the hashed state'. Reviewer must decide whether unread config fields are security-relevant; the test only needs to show the contradiction. Test idea (bugs/<ID>/test.lua): create from bugs/harness/work/configs/baremetal-minimal, run(1000), store, load; assert get_initial_config().processor.registers.mcycle == read_reg('mcycle') and .pc == read_reg('pc'); also after a send_cmio_response on a template, imcyclemax and iflags_Y; exit 1 if they differ (today mcycle 0 vs 1000, pc 0x80000000 vs 0x80000020). Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r7/MANLUA1/t1.lua.

threat_model_gaps: Trailing data in tournament proofs: section 8's Medium case 'A referee verifier that accepts trailing data that does not affect its result (R3)' names verifiers and R3 speaks of transition logs; it is unclear whether ignored computation-hash proof data in the tournament's seal move (Dave _requireAgreeState at leaf 0) counts (R7-MANTOURN-1; same split as R1-R3-3).

Dispute constants versus the normative model: section 5 makes the manual's model normative except listed simplifications and clock values, but does not say whether its demonstration dispute constants (sampling period 2^10) are normative or deployment-chosen; Dave's released period is 2^18 (R7-MANTOURN-2).

Incomplete manual specifications of a transition: unclear whether a manual description that lists a transition's writes but omits some (the delivery's imcyclemax write and rx-buffer zero padding) is a 'contradiction between the manual and the behavior' or silence (R1-R14-2 held silence is not covered), and whether the threat model's own section 2 definition of imcyclemax supplies the missing specification (R7-MANARCH-1).

Non-PRT verification recipes: unclear whether the manual's 'blockchain way' recipes for template instantiation and NVRAM result extraction stand in for an in-scope referee verifier (section 3 support stand-in rule; readings.md asks to check that the stood-in role exists), and whether a helper whose API leaves the root and index binding to its caller is itself a verifier defect (R7-MANHASHSTATE-1).

Verifiers run on proofs received from others outside the honest operator's path: unclear whether a reference output-proof verifier stands in for a referee verifier, for the honest operator's 'may decline' path, or for nothing when its documented walk-through only uses the reader's own artifacts (R7-MANHASHCOMP-1).

Host faults that delete rather than corrupt: section 4 and the host-fault exclusion forbid turning a host fault into 'a directory that O2 guarantees but that later loads as a different state', which does not literally cover error handling that deletes an O2-guaranteed directory, while section 5 forbids damaging one (R7-MANCLIROLL-1).

The uarch memory map: R3 defines a uarch trap by 'an access that its memory map does not allow', but the manual's only description of that map ('access all memory ranges and devices visible to the main processor') does not say whether loads from device MMIO addresses or unmapped holes are allowed (native returns 0), so whether accepting them is a High trap-acceptance defect is undecided (R7-MANARCH-3, related to R1-R10-1).

Non-hash metadata of a stored directory: unclear whether section 8's Medium case 'leaves ... a stored directory inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9)' covers fields that are never read for a transition or hash (config.json register values), and why an on-path operation with the same inconsistency but no named rule violated would rate lower than the off-path Medium case (R7-MANLUA1-2).

Uarch-internal deviations: unclear whether the Medium case 'An undocumented deterministic deviation ... in behavior that no correct guest relies on (R7)' applies to behavior of the uarch that no guest can observe (R7-MANARCH-3).
